_doc: Accepted survivors for scripts/local-ci/guard-ablation.mjs (M-5a/A2).
A SURVIVOR is a mutation of a validator's execute() that leaves every fixture in
its pack producing the same frozen `expected` — i.e. the rule it touched is pinned
by nothing. A new survivor is a HARD CI FAILURE: it means a rule shipped without a
fixture that fails when the rule is reverted alone.
Two classes, and the difference is the whole point of the file:
class: equivalent  the mutation provably CANNOT change execute()'s output for any
input. A permanent entry. Its `reason` must carry the proof, not
an observation that no fixture happened to notice.
class: unpinned    the mutation CAN change output for some input, but no fixture
exercises it. This is DEBT. It must carry an `owner` naming the
work package that closes it, and the total is capped by
`unpinned_budget` below.
Rules, all enforced by the tool (SC-14/A4a — before that it enforced only the first
two, and read neither `class` nor `owner`):
1. a survivor absent from `accepted` fails the gate;
2. an `accepted` entry that is no longer a survivor ALSO fails the gate, so a
stale exemption cannot outlive the gap it excused. Delete it in the same
commit that kills the mutant;
3. every entry carries `reason` and a valid `class`;
4. every `unpinned` entry carries a non-empty `owner`;
5. the number of `unpinned` entries may not exceed `unpinned_budget`. Raising that
number is a deliberate edit in the same commit, the same discipline as
parity/skill-line-budget.json.
SC-14/A4 history (F-86). Audit M-6 found all 19 entries carrying class `unpinned` and
owner 'SC-12 (unscheduled)' — a bulk assignment, not per-entry triage — while the tool
read neither field, so neither the debt nor the lapsed owner had any consequence. A
931-input sweep across both gating modes re-triaged the drift-sentinel entries. It found
exactly one genuinely unpinned AND reachable rule, the legacy YELLOW band: the fixture
named legacy-yellow-zone.json has entropy 0.25, giving ctm 0.08, which lands in the RED
band — a fixture named for a rule it does not pin, which is F-71's exact shape.
legacy-yellow-band-reached.json now pins it and that entry is deleted.
Entries reclassified `equivalent` carry a structural proof. Entries left `unpinned` are
NOT thereby claimed reachable — the sweep is evidence, not proof, and an unreachability
argument that spans function boundaries can be invalidated by a later edit. Leaving them
as debt fails closed, which is the direction this register should fail in.
Scope note: the CLI wrapper at the foot of each validator is NOT mutated.
The parity fixtures call execute() directly via exec-one.js and never invoke the
CLI, so they pin no wrapper line by construction — the first run of this tool
reported nine survivors and all nine were wrapper guards. The wrapper is pinned
instead by parity/cli-contract/run-tests.js (all four exit-3 paths and both input
modes, per validator) and by scripts/local-ci/cli-block-lint.mjs (the nine copies
cannot drift). See the header of guard-ablation.mjs.
Known limitation (recorded SC-14/A4): `mutation` is TRUNCATED with an ellipsis for long
conditions, so an entry cannot always be replayed from this file alone. Two entries
(drift-sentinel:guard-off:#0 and #20) could not be re-triaged for that reason.

why_this_scope: M-5b/B6 extended the sweep from three packs to nine on M-5a/A2's MEASURED cost
(18 mutants / 122 calls / 6 ms for three packs), not on an estimate. Nine packs cost
109 mutants / 1,446 calls / 47 ms -- cheap enough that narrowing buys nothing.
The wider operator catalogue (guard-on, boundary flips, constant offsets, negation,
dropped pushes) is still NOT adopted: the two shipped operators already surfaced 19
unpinned rules, and adding operators before those are closed would grow this list
faster than anyone works it down. Revisit when `accepted` is near empty.
execution-report.js is the largest unswept surface in the repo (~1,400 lines, 24
fixture job-trees) and SC-11's own first-cut fixtures were vacuous there. It needs a
different mechanism -- mutating a report generator means rebuilding job trees, not
calling execute(input) -- so it is named as the next candidate rather than bolted on.
SC-17/F-90 added execution-report.js, and the paragraph above predicted the cost wrong.
It said the file "needs a different mechanism -- mutating a report generator means
rebuilding job trees, not calling execute(input)". Half right. The case RUNNER does
differ: a case is a job directory compared against a frozen golden, not a JSON input
compared against a frozen `expected`. But nothing had to be rebuilt. buildReport(jobDir)
already returns {report, markdown} and writes nothing -- generateExecutionReport is the
thin writing wrapper around it -- so the seam the validators expose as execute(input)
was already there, and the 29 job trees the report suite maintains are the corpus. The
estimate that deferred this sweep was made without reading for the seam.
Two operators still, unchanged. Adding execution-report.js surfaced 20 survivors against
the same two, which is the same argument as before for not widening the catalogue yet:
close what is listed before looking for more.
The report target compares BOTH the report object and the rendered markdown. Comparing
the object alone was the first cut, and the measurement refuted it -- 12 of the 31
survivors that produced were inside renderMarkdown, and they were real: nothing in this
repo asserts markdown CONTENT, since run-tests.js compares run 1 against run 2, which is
determinism rather than correctness. Adding the markdown goldens killed 11 of them.

note: The nine-pack sweep found 19 unpinned rules across six validators no scope change had
ever swept. They are recorded rather than fixed: closing them means new fixtures in
four more packs, each requiring a version bump and a refreeze -- validator work, and
M-5b changes no validator. Recording converts 19 invisible gaps into 19 tracked ones
that CI will not let anyone forget, and the rule is bidirectional: an entry that stops
surviving fails the gate until it is deleted.
Superseded as the current figure by `measured_sc17` below; kept as the nine-pack record.
The `execute_calls: 1446` above has the same defect the SC-17 review found in
measured_sc17: it is mutants x fixtures, counted before each mutant ran, not calls made.
Left as recorded history rather than re-derived -- doing so would mean re-running a version
of the tool that no longer exists. Read it as a matrix size. The same caveat applies to the
M-5a "122 calls" figure quoted in guard-ablation.mjs's header comment.

unpinned_budget_doc: Cap on `class: unpinned` entries (SC-14/A4a). May only be raised by a deliberate edit in the same commit, with the reason in the commit message and the new entry's `owner`. Lowering it is free and is the point.

PROVEN EQUIVALENT (SC-14/A4). Algebraic identity, not a coverage gap. The branch IS reachable (any all-zero signal window enters it), but when max === 0 every element of `abs` is already 0, so `abs.map(() => 0)` and the fall-through are the same array — and the fall-through is reached, because `max <= 1` holds for 0. Both paths return identical values, so no fixture can distinguish them and none should be written.

No fixture carries an Advocate resolution whose `action` is unrecognized. Deleting the guard admits any string as a resolution action and every golden is unchanged, so nothing proves the whitelist is read.

The tolerant-reader skip in firstFindingIssue (artifact-layout rule 8). No fixture has a null or non-object entry inside `critic.findings`, so the one input the guard exists for never arrives — deleted, a null entry would throw rather than be skipped.
The same tolerant-reader skip in firstFindingText, unreached for the same reason. Two copies of one rule, both unpinned; a single fixture with a malformed findings entry closes both.
Needs a Critic finding carrying `issue` with no `evidence`. Every fixture finding has both, so the fallback ladder in firstFindingText is only ever entered at its first rung.
The other rung of the same ladder: a finding carrying `evidence` with no `issue`. Same cause, same one-fixture fix.

The pipeline_completion gate FAILS a job that produced all seven phases but never reached `completed`. No fixture is both complete in evidence and incomplete in status, so the branch is unreached. Worth naming precisely: this is the half of the gate SC-16/F-88b had to reason about — the "did this run finish" question as distinct from "did it lose a phase" — and that reasoning was done against a branch no test covers.
phase_gates returns UNVERIFIED when no phase attempt was recorded at all. Every fixture has at least a plan attempt — verified by scanning all 29 goldens for an empty `phases` array.

F-5's rule: a ship gate still `deferred` at the terminal report is a delegated push nobody closed. promote_delegated_push records the CLOSED shape, so the still-open shape this WARN exists for is untested.

grader_verdict returns UNVERIFIED when a verify attempt exists but its rubric_result is absent or unrecognized. Fixtures either have no verify attempt (an earlier return) or a well-formed verdict, so the middle case never occurs.
consensus returns UNVERIFIED with no rounds recorded. No golden has an empty `consensus` array — verified across all 29 — so a job that ran no consensus round is a shape the corpus does not contain.
No fixture records `final_status: "quarantined"`. The whole branch, including its decision_reason, is unreached; every QUARANTINE verdict in the corpus arrives through gate evaluation instead.

The quarantine-class split inside the `failed` branch. No fixture pairs `final_status: "failed"` with a QUARANTINE_REASONS member, so the non-retriable half of that rule is untested while the retriable half is pinned.

No fixture records `final_status: "canceled"`. Sharply worth naming: SC-16/F-88 exists BECAUSE three live runs were forced to record a halt as a cancel, and the branch they were forced into is pinned by nothing. The `halted` branch beside it now has three fixtures.
renderMarkdown's empty-phases placeholder. Unreachable for the same reason as guard-off:#23; one zero-attempt fixture closes both.
renderMarkdown's empty-consensus placeholder. Pairs with guard-off:#33 and closes with the same fixture.

buildReport throws INVALID_JOB_DIR when run_manifest.json is missing or unreadable. The CLI error-path case covers a missing DIRECTORY, which returns earlier from main(); a directory that exists with no readable manifest is a different path and has no case.
Removes 'warn' from the set of grader verdicts the gate recognizes. No fixture records a grader rubric_result of 'warn', so the corpus cannot tell a recognized warn from an unrecognized value.
The WARN arm of the grader verdict mapping, unreached for the same reason: with no 'warn' grader verdict anywhere in the corpus, a three-way mapping is only ever exercised two ways.

hasGateStatus's defensive non-array guard. Through buildReport — the only entry point this target sweeps — `gates` is always the seven-element array literal constructed a few lines above the call, so the mutation provably cannot change any output reachable here. Classified equivalent rather than unpinned because no fixture could close it without calling the exported decideLifecycle directly, which is a different claim from the one this tool makes. If a future target ever does call it that way, this entry becomes killable and the bidirectional STALE check reports it.

note: execution-report.js alone: 109 mutants x 29 report fixtures, 19 survivors. 90 of its
109 mutants are KILLED, which is the number that says the target is wired up rather
than merely quiet -- a target where everything survives is a misconfiguration, not a
file without rules.
Wall clock went 47 ms -> 1,202 ms, a 25x rise, and it is still the second-cheapest step
in the gate. The report target does real directory I/O per call where the validators are
pure in-memory; that is the whole difference. Measured before deciding placement, so it
stays in Tier 1.
The budget moved 16 -> 34. Eighteen of the new entries are unpinned debt owned by SC-18
and one is equivalent. One survivor was CLOSED rather than accepted:
skills_clean’s "a skill invocation failed" branch, which six fixtures appeared to cover
and none reached -- every one of them returns from the SC-8/F-58 mismatch branch or the
SC-11 unreadable-evidence branch first. quarantine_skill_fail is the fixture that
reaches it, and it took the corpus from 28 to 29.
Every pre-existing unpinned entry was re-owned SC-15 -> SC-18. SC-15 shipped as PR #81
two work packages ago, so the owner field was stale for the SECOND time (F-86 was the
first, when 19 entries named an already-shipped SC-12). Rule 4 asserts the field is a
non-empty string and cannot assert the package is still open, so this will go stale a
third time unless something checks it. Named here rather than fixed here.
The call figure was corrected in review. `execute_calls` here first read 4,867, which was
mutants x fixtures -- a CEILING, accumulated before each mutant ran, while both runners
short-circuit on the first case that disagrees. The measured figure is 2,202, so the first
cut overstated by 2.2x, and the label was wrong besides: the report target calls
buildReport(), not execute(). Both numbers are kept, because the RATIO is the interesting
one -- ceiling and measured diverge more the better the corpus is, since a well-pinned rule
dies on its first case and never reaches the rest. Reported as work performed, the ceiling
reads highest exactly when the suite is doing its job.
measured_case_runs is ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT and 2,202 is this host, not an invariant. As root
-- which the containerised cross-version legs are -- quarantine_unreadable_manifest is skipped,
because mode 000 is still readable there, so every mutant that reaches the end of the corpus
runs one case fewer: Node 20 in the orb container measures 2,181. Survivor counts, mutant counts
and verdicts are identical across both. Compare those, not this.
